title: Decimals
objectives: Understand decimal place values (tenths, hundredths, thousandths)
Add, subtract, multiply, and divide decimals

introduction.context: Decimals are used everywhere in real life - money ($3.45), measurements (2.5 meters), and scientific data. They're another way to represent parts of wholes, just like fractions.
introduction.connection: Decimals are closely related to fractions from Chapter 5. For example, 0.5 = 1/2 and 0.25 = 1/4.

concepts.title: Decimal Place Values
concepts.content: Decimal places continue the place value system to the right of the decimal point: tenths, hundredths, thousandths, and so on.

concepts.title: Adding and Subtracting Decimals
concepts.content: To add or subtract decimals, line up the decimal points and add or subtract as with whole numbers. The decimal point in the answer goes directly below the others.

commonErrors: Forgetting to add zeros as placeholders

hints: Both numbers have the same place value
No borrowing needed for this problem
